h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A third serial 3x3 on the deep path hits diminishing returns and harder optimization under the short NB201 training schedule.
A second identity-like route into node 3 duplicates gradient flow and dilutes conv branches in the output sum, shrinking the shortcut's marginal value.
With a conv-only deep route into node 3, the edge-3 residual becomes the main clean gradient path, raising its marginal value.
Pooling an identity-fed node 1 merely blurs the raw input with no learned features to aggregate.
When edge 0 already supplies spatial context to node 1, a 1x1 on edge 4 loses little relative to alternatives, so it fares better than when node 1 is unprocessed.
Parallel shallow conv routes into node 3 substitute for each other, so a second one adds largely redundant capacity.
Without the node-1-to-output edge, node 1 contributes only via the deep path where edge 0 is the capacity bottleneck.
A conv in parallel with an identity-fed route gives node 2 complementary features, whereas parallel with a conv it is redundant.
With the input shortcut replaced by a conv, a node-2 identity restores residual gradient flow into the output.
Pooling on both inputs to the deep path leaves node 2 dominated by blurred features, compounding oversmoothing.
